review.rationale: Methodological contract for Test Card T025 (T023 repeated with a phylogenetic correction). The evidence decision lives in docs/standard. Longevity, metabolic rate and body mass as compiled in AnAge; the TimeTree tree is local-only because TimeTree does not allow redistribution.

question: With species related by a phylogeny (PGLS, Brownian motion), do bats spend about as much energy per gram over a lifetime as birds?

output.quantity: bat offset d_bat and Delta = d_bat - d_bird in log10 LEP
output.domain: AnAge Build 15 Aves and Mammalia as in T018/T023, placed on a TimeTree 5 tree (285 of 298 species)
output.accuracy: 95 percent t-intervals from generalized least squares with the Brownian-motion covariance of the TimeTree tree.

model.assumptions: tau = F/P with the reserve per gram set at species level by extrinsic mortality; flight lowers extrinsic mortality (author statement 2026-11-18, AI translation).
model.approximation: Resting metabolic rate stands for lifetime expenditure; maximum longevity stands for tau.
model.drive_environment: Captive and wild records as compiled in AnAge.
model.parameters: No fitting decides the outcome; the prediction is s = 0 and d = 0.

data_policy.holdout_policy: No holdout. AnAge values seen in T023 (SEEN_FULL); tree leaf names, count and root age read before approval (SEEN_SUMMARY); declared in Test Card T025.

system_partition.boundary: Species-level records compiled in AnAge; published values used only.

state_accounting.rule: One record per species as compiled.

couplings.map: Longevity records and respirometry compiled from the literature

observables.quantity: maximum longevity; metabolic rate; body mass

observation.source_state: Adult animals as recorded in the cited studies.
observation.readout: Maximum longevity (yr), metabolic rate (W), body mass (g).

components.reason: Applied upstream in the studies compiled by AnAge; not recomputed here.

LEP, species placement on the tree, PGLS fit and t-intervals; outcome rule fixed in T025.
Cholesky-whitened least squares (numpy), Student t quantiles and bounded likelihood maximisation for Pagel's lambda (scipy).

error_budget.numerical: Direct linear algebra; no Monte Carlo error.
error_budget.approximation: Resting rate instead of lifetime expenditure; maximum longevity instead of typical lifespan.
error_budget.measurement: Species records carry no stated errors; residual variance estimated from the PGLS fit.
error_budget.systematic: Field/resting metabolic ratio may differ between classes; captive and wild longevity mixed; bat torpor inflates resting-rate LEP; tree is a TimeTree summary without branch-length uncertainty.
error_budget.omissions: Reptiles, fish and other classes not used.
error_budget.dependence: Handled by the Brownian-motion covariance; Pagel's lambda reported, not deciding.
error_budget.acceptance: Outcome categories fixed in Test Card T025.

claim_boundary: Methodological coverage of the T025 comparison only; the evidence level is set in docs/standard. Not UET-distinct: the nearest theory is disposable soma and the extrinsic-mortality theory of ageing.
next_action: Field metabolic rates or a torpor-aware bat subset would need their own Test Card; they cannot change the T025 outcome.
